If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.

If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to compensate for bearish bias.

If sentiment shifts from negative to positive over 3–5 days, adjust forecast upward by 1–2% in mid-horizon (8–15 days) to capture momentum reversal.

If sentiment remains flat (0.33–0.67) across 5+ days, apply no correction to forecast in late horizon (16–30 days) — residual error is typically stochastic and non-structural.

If sentiment spikes to 1.00 in last 2 days, reduce forecast by 1–2% in late horizon (20–30 days) to prevent overcorrection from recent bullish momentum.

If sentiment drops to 0.00 in last 2 days, increase forecast by 1–2% in mid-horizon (10–20 days) to offset potential market underreaction.
